research_answers.Q1_important_bit_planes: Bit planes 15 through 8 (MSBs) carry >95% of numerical significance. Dropping MSBs (15, 14, 13) causes immediate quality collapse.
research_answers.Q2_IEEE_ordering_match: IEEE 754 floating-point bit order generally matches inference importance, though exponent bit planes (14..10) exhibit higher sensitivity than fraction bits.
research_answers.Q3_sensitive_layers: Middle transformer layers (layers 12-20) and final layer norms exhibit highest activation error sensitivity under low precision.
research_answers.Q4_sensitive_tensors: LM Head and Embedding tensors exhibit highest numerical precision sensitivity, followed by Attention Q/V projections.
research_answers.Q5_error_origin: Error originates in fraction truncation at low bits, cascading from weight MAE into activation divergence and logit shift.
research_answers.Q6_collapse_point: Precision collapse begins strictly at 6 bits and below (<8 bits shows quality drop, <6 bits experiences total collapse).
